newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi wins lower house vote of confidence.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi wins lower house vote of confidence.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi survived a vote of confidence in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) after his hard-left ally broke ranks and defied the government on a security force for Albania.

The centre-left government won the do-or-die vote by 321 votes to 166. Prodi was forced into the test after needing opposition support to approve the Albania mission and overcame a similar vote on Thursday in the Senate (upper house).

The hard-left Communist Refoundation party, which secures the coalition's majority in the lower house, returned to government ranks after defying Prodi over the Albanian mission, which is due to swing into action next week.

Addressing the Chamber earlier on Saturday, Prodi said his coalition government would no longer brook such dissent, saying he needed a cohesive majority if he was to carry out a promised reform of the welfare state.
"For this reason we cannot have other wrenches as serious as this one. They will no longer be accepted," Prodi said.

Prodi came to power last May but has always struggled to get along with his troublesome Marxist ally. Other coalition partners have threatened to quit the government if Prodi fails to reach an accord with Refoundation on future policy goals.
